text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit I’m a big fan of the Thames & Kosmos building kits--especially the ones that teach STEM principles. However, this THAMES & KOSMOS PEPPER MINT IN THE FANTASTIC UNDERWATER SCIENCE VOYAGE EXPERIMENT KIT is definitely NOT one of my favorites. The experiments do teach about the physical properties of water (e.g., siphoning, hydraulics), but they are boring--mostly they require operating a syringe to push water through tubing.

The boat is easy to build. The parts are stamped onto thin sheets of wood. You punch the parts out of the sheets, and the edges come out smooth and clean. The parts then lock together without requiring glue or other fasteners. The assembly instructions are included in a booklet that contains a silly adventure/discovery story that features the girl character Pepper Mint.

The story is interrupted from time to time with instructions for science experiments. Each experiment has a good, easy-to-understand explanation of “what’s happening” (e.g., water can move things because, unlike air, it cannot be compressed).

The kit is apparently aimed at 11-year-old girls (Pepper Mint’s age), but the story and the experiments seem rather simplistic for that age group. I do wish that Thames & Kosmos had chosen a more serious name than “Pepper Mint” for their girl scientist. This kit has some teaching value, but it trivializes science for girls.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Pepper Mint in The Fantastic Underwater Science Voyage Experiment Kit

So, if you misplace any pieces, then you really have to throw the whole thing away, or put it in your junk plastic pile. But, those are the only two negative things.

The car elevator has a place you can lift up, and that's really fun for little kids, especially ones that are still learning motor skills. The car that mine came with is really cool, but I think there's a different car in every set. Overall it's a great set.

text_fidelity_a:
Money Savvy Pig - Pink Money Savvy Pig offers a fun and effective way to teach kids about money and its many important uses. Parents devote very little time to the concept of financial management, in spite of its critical nature, often because they are not sure how best to approach the subject. Money Savvy Pig makes it easy to introduce youngsters to these important concepts.

How does Money Savvy Pig work as an educational device? The answer is simple. By including four different chambers with different labels- one for spend, one for save, one for donate, and one for invest- kids gain a sense of financial management and money allocation. They learn that money has uses that go far beyond ordinary spending. Kids under the age of seven are not ready to learn the specifics of these different concepts, but early exposure is a good idea and the Money Savvy Bank Pig certainly succeeds in this respect.

The Money Savvy Bank is made from plastic and mine has held up fine thus far. Others have pointed out that this bank can break if dropped on a hard surface. Considering its lightweight design, it isn't difficult to imagine the bank breaking apart if mishandled, which is why parents need to exercise caution and make sure their kids handle the bank with extra care when moving from one place to the next.

I like that this bank separates money into four different sections and I like that it gets kids thinking about money and its uses. One limitation, however, is that this bank isn't very good for storing paper money. The reason is because the pieces of paper are difficult to remove. The openings on the bottom of the bank are small- too small to stick your hand inside the bank to remove paper. Place a folded dollar bill inside this bank and it will take some shaking and maneuvering to remove it from the bottom. Thus, this bank should be avoided for storing paper currency. It is intended for use with coins.

Financial literacy is important and kids need to learn about money at the youngest age possible. The Money Savvy Pig is a very good piggy bank for youngsters and its benefits go far beyond the encouragement of savings. It encourages kids to ask questions and think about money in different ways, making it a great choice for a child's early financial education.
text_fidelity_b: Money Savvy Pig - Pink

Adora Playtime Collection Pink 13 Soft Baby Doll with Bottle This is a sweet, tiny baby girl doll about half the size of your average newborn. I expected the feet, hands, and head to be ever so slightly softer than they are, but it's not so hard that you'd be upset if you fell over on it or had your big brother bash you with it, hopefully accidentally.

The baby powder fragrance is a little overwhelming to start, but I'm hoping that will settle down in time. I'm not really used to a lot of artificial fragrances so it's definitely a lot stronger than any other scented item in our home. The fragrance is overall pleasant, just a little too much. It really sticks to your hands, too. I played with the doll for just a few minutes with my son, and after washing my hands twice with Dr. Bronner's peppermint soap, I can still smell the artificial baby powder fragrance.

The baby bottle included doesn't look very realistic in the sense that the entire thing is made of a pale pink plastic, so there's nothing that looks "milky" in there. There's also no differentiation between nipple, lid, and bottle. That said, it does fit into the baby's mouth and stay there nicely. I like that the baby's body is made of the silky material kind of like a ribbon, and the outfit she is wearing is easy to take off and put on for little hands. I wish there was not printing on the front of the shirt, as I'm not sure a baby doll needs to say "pretty girl" on the front. My son really enjoys taking off the headband and putting it back on.

The eyes open and close and if not perfectly upright, the baby has a generally heavy lidded disposition. The one unnerving thing is that when the eyes are opened/the baby is angled too quickly, the eyes make a clicking sound when the lids open fully. I wish they'd done a little more design testing to eliminate that minor flaw, because my toddler son was immediately entranced and wondered what the noise was and it caused some not very gentle experimentation with flipping the baby around to see what was going on with the sound.

Even with what I see as a few minor design flaws, overall this is a very sweet, nicely sized baby doll for a young one aged 1 to 3, and would be a good doll to put in a miniature baby carrier or generally to carry around and play with. I wish I had thought to get a doll like this prior to my son's baby sister arriving so that he could practice playing gently with doll and nurturing the doll.

LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces) This LEGO CREATOR EXPERT VESTAS WIND TURBINE BUILDING KIT (10268; 826 Piece) is a fascinating set that’s much more fun than the advertising makes it appear. Its best feature is also its greatest drawback--the huge turbine blades take a lot of space to display and operate. The blades are motorized (with a servo hidden in the “Vestas” box at the top), and when they’re turning, the two house entrance lights turn on. What better way to dramatize the point that a single huge wind turbine can power thousands of homes?

The model is slightly challenging to build, because it calls for a lot of studs-not-on-top assembly. It’s especially interesting to see how the heavy wind turbine assemblage is secured to the base with only LEGO elements. The set does use specialized large green elements around the shaft to hide the battery box and to help hold the wind turbine firmly.

The model also demonstrates the one feature that bothers me about wind turbines as a source of electricity--they are huge, and loom over their surrounding landscape. The little house is dwarfed by the wind turbine. The house is cute, with windows and door that open, a range and sink, a lamp on a table, and a patio with a table and chairs (created from “repurposed” wheel-well elements).

The minifigs (two Vestas engineers, a female homeowner, and a dog) are great. The engineers have a van that holds their work bench and a hand truck loaded with service tanks and a big assortment of tools. The instruction book includes several pages describing the development of wind turbines as a power source, and showing diagrams of how they work to create electricity from wind currents.

The wind turbine on the model can be rotated by hand atop the shaft. Only the wind turbine blades are motorized. The blades are operated by a switch at the bottom of the shaft. The motor and lights run on 6 AA batteries (not included). The trees in the set are made from plants. (My LEGO Wind Turbine set was purchased from a LEGO Shop.)
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert Vestas Wind Turbine 10268 Building Kit (826 Pieces)

Imhotep Builder of Egypt | Family Board Game by Kosmos | 2-4 Players | Ages 10+ | Toy of The Year Finalist | Parents Choice Gold Award Winner | Toy Insider Top Holiday Toy | Spiel Des Jahres-Nominated This is just a first-time playing review, which I'll update as we continue to play. But at this point it wouldn't surprise me if the score gets bumped up to a five.

Components: high quality. They seem quite well made, durable, and are beautiful looking.

Set up: Set up is pretty easy and quick despite the number of materials (we played with three)

Gameplay: Deceptively simple. Your goal is to build structures using blocks which you quarry then place on a boat then sail to one of four places then unload them, with various points scored at the ends of rounds and the game depending on what you achieved. It is, as mentioned, deceptively simple because though you only have a few options, the other players of course get to do their own thing, which often involves blocking your thing. So that ship you were planning to load up with that particular stone you needed? Somebody just decided to sail it away. Those stone you loaded on that ship to build a pyramid? Somebody docked it instead at the obelisk area. So you need to work around what your opponents are doing, try to anticipate what they're going to do, as well as try to block them as well. It's fun, frustrating, stimulating, engaging, and did I mention fun?

We really enjoyed playing it even with the usual slow-down issues of playing a game for the first time. Even with those first game issues, the game was finished in under an hour and I would imagine you could get through it in 30 minutes regularly. An additional plus is that although the game will play differently lots of times obviously with all the variations on situations, the game itself comes with a "B" side (in other words, its own variant)

I'll update as we get more games under our hat, but right now Imhotep seems like a winner

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

text_fidelity_a:
VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version Kids like to do grown- up things and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera allows them to do just that. This is a fully- functioning camera specifically designed for the needs and desires of youngsters and it allows kids to take pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even upload them to a computer for further viewing and editing.

Many qualities make this camera one to consider and the first is the memory. This is sold as a child's camera, but it has a surprisingly high level of memory and is capable of holding up to 400 pictures! This is much better than I expected and with this much memory, it will take a long time before kids exceed the available space. They can walk around the house ansd snap picture after picture without worrying that the memory will fill.

Another positive aspect with the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is its durability. This camera is made from plastic with a rubberized edge that makes it easy to hold and highly resistant to breakage. My girls have dropped it several times and it continues to work regardless. It is also very entertaining. Not only can kids take their own pictures of mom, dad, the family dog, and their friends, but they can also add to the fun by using the editing feature. The silly editing allows kids a chance to take an ordinary picture and make it look funny.

So, the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is fun for kids, but are there any cons? Well, there are a few but they are minor enough to overlook. One is the viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is quite small and some images will be barely perceptible. It would be completely unacceptable to adults, but kids will likely find it perfectly fine. Then, one has to consider the picture quality. This camera has only 0.3 megapixels and that means the clarity of the pictures is well below average. Once again, kids are not likely to care. They will so enjoy having their own camera and taking their own pictures that they won't even notice or mind the fuzzy images.

Kids like to mimic adults and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is likely to be a hit with most youngsters for this and other reasons. As I said, the clarity of the photos isn't the best and the camera does have a few other minor flaws, but none of this will matter to most children. The ability to take their own pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even view them on a computer will be more than enough to please the young camerabug in your home.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version

Friends TV Show Collage Jigsaw Puzzle 1000 Pieces Officially Licensed Friends TV Show Merchandise EDIT: initially I reviewed this before really getting into the puzzle. I’m in it now, and I can say this is one of the most poorly formulated puzzles I’ve ever done. It appears that whoever decided the pattern of the piece cut outs was lazy and decided to have repeating shapes throughout, which results in many perfect fits that are completely incorrect. In places where the differences are obvious, it’s not much of an issue, but there are also plenty of times this happens in areas that look similar, resulting in incorrect placement, backtracking, and frustration. I love puzzles, but not this one. I love friends, but I can’t stand this friends puzzle. The visual design was excellent, so whoever came up with that did a wonderful job. Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

So the puzzle itself isn’t super high res, nor are the pieces particularly inventive in how they’re cut, but man am I having fun reliving the show. Honestly, this is all about the nostalgia and having a chill time. It’s a little harder than I expected, but still totally doable. Perfect escape!

B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z Toddlers love to play and they benefit from toys that encourage learning or help in other areas of development. One toy that seems promising in these ways is the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers.

This puzzle has knobs on the pieces, making it easy for toddlers to grab each piece. It helps with coordination, too, as little ones will learn to fit the right shape into the right slot. However, the colors of the pieces are washed out and they really need to be an eye catching primary. Not only would it be more inviting to toddlers and preschoolers but it would provide an opportunity to not only teach numbers and counting, but color recognition too while playing.

Another issue with the pieces is that the details are lacking. If you are going to add detail make it something a child can recognize. But probably the most shocking oversight is the shapes and numbers that they are supposed to match. There is an octagon, for example, that represents the number 7, a five- pointed star that is used for the number 8, and so on. Why would you do this? The octagon should be the number 8 and the star should match with number 5. This is an oversight that someone should have caught.

Other issues I have are with the puzzle holes- they are a little too big and this would be hard to travel anywhere with. I do like that the numbers are nice and big and easy to see and that the knobs are big and tall enough for tiny fingers to grasp. While I haven’t seen it happen yet I do worry because, since they are very much like thumbtacks, they may come loose and eventually get lost. The pieces don’t hold in place as well as I would like.

Toddler toys that help kids learn are nice and while the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers does help with coordination and other skills, it lacks in other areas. The oversight with the numbers and shapes not matching is a big one and I have other issues, too. So, when I think of everything as a whole, this toy gets a thumbs down from me.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z

Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces) The Mega Construx Kadabra is better suited for display rather than actual play. His hands fall off quite easily. The play feature of the purple orb is pretty meh. But due to his ball and socket joints, he stands without needing assistance or to lean against anything.

Assembly takes about 30 minutes. The instructions are clear; the hardest part is often clicking the pieces together. My fingers actually hurt after I was finished, due to the pressure I needed to exert to get some of the pieces to fit together. I’ve noticed this with other Mega Construx sets. I wish they would fix this, as it makes it harder for young kids to do this on their own.

The set is rated 6+, which I would say is accurate for the instructions and building. The main difficulty will be snapping pieces together. I had imprints on my fingers -- that’s how hard it can be to get some pieces to fit. Which is ironic, considering how easily some other pieces, like Kadabra’s hands, fall off the finished Pokémon.

The printing on his face and chest is a lighter pink than it appears on the box.

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. This way you can ensure it’s evenly lined up.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

CTSC 75FT 95FT 110FT 250FT Zipline Kit with Stainless Steel Spring Brake and Seat My kids love this. I had a couple of trees a bit over a hundred feet apart on a shallow incline, which seemed pretty perfect.

I did end up putting this together and taking it apart about ten times before I was satisfied with it, so I definitely dumped more time than I intended into it. Making adjustments is often almost as big a job as starting from scratch. The loop at the top of the line was small, and that wanted to attach to a giant redwood, so I had to switch trees, though I'm sure I could've bought a longer section of cable. The bottom end seems like it would be able to handle a big tree fine. Maybe I could've swapped ends, but it doesn't indicate that as an option anywhere. The instructions are a bit sparse, but mostly sufficient. I hadn't realized initially that the big velcro pads had a slot for the cable to go through to keep it from slipping off the pad. By the time I got everything attached high enough, I had a lot of trouble pulling all of the slack out of the line. The turnbuckle was way too short for the task. I eventually had to get creative with clamps and bungee cords to get enough mechanical advantage to pull it tight enough to clamp it down.

The included seat is nice for when you want both adults and kids to be able to use it. It allows it to be attached up high enough to be out of the way and usable by adults, while still being low enough for smaller kids to ride on the seat. My kids use it more than the trampoline, so it's a hit.

The drone flew up a few feet but also flew forward (or backwards) even though I wasn’t touching the right control stick which is supposed to do that. Up and down seemed to be working fine, but with the drone constantly flying sideways, it was impossible to control properly. Even when using the right control stick, it seemed to only acknowledge forwards, and wouldn’t respond to the other direction. Then the drone suddenly dropped the WiFi connection within 10 minutes. Powering off and on didn’t fix it. I took the battery out, put it back in and was connected again for a minute or two before the battery just died completely. Yes, I fully charged the battery before use. Surely this products battery should last more than 15 minutes of intermittent usage.
Overall, as someone familiar with remote control devices and technology, I found this drone difficult to control and hence no fun to use.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA X22W Mini Drone with Camera Live Video FPV Pocket Drone for Kids and Beginners, RC Quadcopter with App Control, Altitude Hold, 3D Flips, Headless Mode and Bonus Battery, Red

This is a 3D game with levels and "mole hills" to stack.  The setup is easy and sturdy.  You use the bottom of the box as part of the set-up.  All the pieces are well made and strong- not going to be easy to break or fold.  The art and details are amazing.  The instructions are only about 3 pages long- which is short for some of today's games.  They are easy to understand and have illustrations to keep everyone on the same page.  Another wonderful thing is that there are TWO playing modes.  One mode when you only have two people, and another for larger groups.  Games that do this are great- it means you can have as much fun and challenges playing as two people as you can with four.  It suggests ages 9+ because some of the strategy involved, though younger children could play with some guidance.  The objective for this game is to build the mole hills and control the most mountains.  Very fun to play.

Challengers Card Game | Strategy/Interactive Deck Management Game | Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 10+ | 1-8 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Z-Man Games For this game, you really need to know what you're getting.

This is a strategy deckbuilding game with a lot of silly, and a little stupid. And if you're OK with a lot of silly and a little stupid, you will probably love Challengers! if you have a even number of players.

In Challengers, you are deckbuilding in preparation for a game of War. Yes, that game of War where you mindlessly turn over cards and hope for high numbers, even knowing that there are a bunch of low numbers in your deck.

The only player choice is made during the deckbuilding phase, and then you get to sit back and watch the chaos.

And if you're OK with a chaotic game like this, where choices are limited and it's all down to luck, then you've found a winner with Challengers! If you think this sounds like a waste of time, then for you, it probably is. We had a few stand up and cheer come-from-behind moments and a lot of inglorious losses.

This is a great deckbuilding intro for kids, and for the grownups with the right tastes, this will be a hit, but I think a lot of people will absolutely hate it also.
text_fidelity_b: Challengers Card Game | Strategy/Interactive Deck Management Game | Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 10+ | 1-8 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Z-Man Games

text_fidelity_a:
Happy The Birthday Bird Stuffed Plush Animal with Interactive Book – Adorable Book Character Stuffed Animals with Birthday Theme - Soft Cuddly Fabric – Includes Memory Pages, Photo Storing Pocket I have had several friends who have given birth over the last year or so. Many of them have had all sorts of great ideas and things happen. When I saw this set, I knew one in particular had to have it.

WHAT THIS IS LIKE
This is in a really cool gift box as shown in the promo from the company. It is a clear front and the bird, balloon, and book are visible through the window. There is a ribbon handle at the top.

HOW THIS WORKS
This works so that you have the little doll, put the balloon on the doll which goes with the story. You hide a little gift in the bird and the child can have fun looking for it. The book allows you to document this journey every year.

BACK POCKET
The book has a back pocket so that you can put the picture in the book of that year. When the new year comes out, you repeat the journey and then take off the older picture, put it in the back pocket, and then put the newest picture documenting the even in its place.

HOW DO THEY LIKE THIS?
This was so well received. The bird is adorable. There are sparkles in his eyes, the sneakers are red metallic, and the design is appealing and really cute. The little backpack allows for a small gift, but nothing large. This is just what this particular family needed. They wanted to document their baby's growth and have a really alert a curious little one who loves things like this.

ADOPTION
If you happen to be someone who is involved in adoption, this also might be a great way for the open adoption to share the growth of the baby with the birth mom or family. It would be a great bridge between the mom and dear family who adopts the children.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I highly recommend this set. If you have a child age 2 or so you can start the tradition. You can start as a baby, but with restrictions on the journey. It is a really cool tradition to encourage kids to be who they are meant to be, have fun documenting the tradition and keep track of their growth for future reference as a family keep sake.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is endearing and I will be buying more of these for other families that I know who would love it.
text_fidelity_b: Happy The Birthday Bird Stuffed Plush Animal with Interactive Book – Adorable Book Character Stuffed Animals with Birthday Theme - Soft Cuddly Fabric – Includes Memory Pages, Photo Storing Pocket

text_fidelity_a: WE Games 4 Player Shut The Box Dice Board Game with Lid- Walnut Stained Wood - Large Coffee Table Size - 14 Inches, for Family and Adult Game Night Play in Classroom, Home or Bar Product listing says 12 yrs and up. Kids under 12 will love this game, trust me. It's not just adding and subtracting, for more advance play, you can do multiplication, division, any math you can think of. Lets say your roll a 4 and a 3, but you're out of tiles to make 7. But you have a 9 and a 3 in play, well if multiplication is part of the game then 4x3 is 12, hence, you can shut the 9 and 3 tiles. Lets say you roll a 5 and a 4, but you have no more tiles that add up to 9, but you have a 3 in play. What's the square root of 9? It's 3, now you can shut that 3. Any math you can think of is fair game, that's how we play it. Play this game with your kids, and they will learn math faster! 5-Stars.

Terra by Battat – Wild Life Set – Realistic Animal Toy Figures with Elephant Toys for Kids 3+ (6 Pc) This is a great little set of heavier resin animals, that is a much better price point than the ones from Schleich (but definitely not as fine of detail or good quality). The variety on this set is nice, and the animals seem to be all of a similar size to where there are no huge and glaring discrepancies in scale.

The one thing that's a little bit confusing to me as it seems like a few of these animals have a shinier, slicker finish that looks a lot cheaper, while some of the animals have a more matte or hashed texture like for, that looks a lot more like a higher end product. Why the mix? It feels inconsistent and kind of confusing, and had you laid all of these out for me and not told me they were in a set, I would not have guessed that the lion and tiger, for example, went in the same set as the gorilla. It's like there are two levels of quality that were then combined into one set.

That said, my 3 1/2 and 5 1/2-year-old noticed zero deficiencies, and got right to playing. We have a Safari animal Hospital set and these animals went right into the Safari vet clinic and were incorporated into play. They are heavy so not good for kids who are still banging things around, but they are certainly durable and I can see no way that these might possibly break.

Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs) We like the Lego brand, but sometimes we need a lot of bricks without paying an exorbitant amount of money. The 1,100 piece kit from Building Bricks was exactly what we were looking for. The Big Questions:
1. Do they really work well with Lego Brand Legos?
Yes - they work very well. It's difficult to tell the difference if you're not really trying hard.
2. How much cheaper are they? Is it really worth it?
It's hard to compare exact pricing here because this set does not include wheels, doors or special pieces. If I had to choose a product to compare it to, I'd probably compare it with Lego's XXL Classic Box (https://www.amazon.com/10697-Building-Large-Creator-Pieces/dp/B00XJ5C4FW). When pricing per piece, the Lego box is about 5¢ per piece. And yes, you read that right. You're dolling out a nickel for every piece of plastic with Lego's brand stamped on it. :) Building Bricks runs about 3¢ per piece. So the answer is: It's almost half the price - very worth it if you're just needing a lot of standard pieces.
As a side note: We really liked the color choices Building Bricks made. They're perfect for expanding your Lego creation palette.
text_fidelity_b: Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs)

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

It’s absolutely charming, all 6 pieces of it!

I really like the drivers’ windows, with a boy on one side and a girl on the other. It makes this into a truly unisex toy. I love the big blue traffic cone that fits between the drivers’ cabin and the moveable crane for transport. Tow trucks always set out traffic cones, for safety, when they’re readying a tow. The crane itself is fun because it swings up and down freely.

The building instructions are on the outside of the retail box. The toy takes about 30 seconds for an adult to assemble, as the wheels are already attached to the truck base. When the toy is finished, it makes a terrific truck for general play. The wheels turn freely, and the truck feels solid and satisfying when it’s pushed around.

Inside the box is a printed city street layout. The paper is very thin, so this won’t last long unless it’s glued to some sort of heavier backing. However the street layout fits the assembled tow truck, and is a nice detail.

Note that this is a LEGO duplo model, intended for very young children. The pieces are much larger than standard LEGO pieces. They are compatible with other duplo building sets, but NOT with standard LEGO elements.

text_fidelity_a: Kamigami Scarrax Robot - Discontinued by Manufacturer This box weighs next to nothing, and the contents are not particularly impressive when you open the box -- causing me to raise an eyebrow at what seems like a high price.  But after putting this toy together, you realize that you are not paying for the physical materials that make the toy, but rather for the programming that makes the toy fun.  In the box, you will find a flat plastic sheet stamped with eight parts, a bag of teeny-tinyplastic rivets for assembly, a USB charger cable, and some electronic body parts.  It takes a little bit of patience (and steady fingers) to put this the Scarrax together, but it is not particularly difficult, and no special tools are required.  It's mostly a matter of folding the pieces from the plastic sheet and snapping them together with the rivets.  I would allow an hour, at least, for getting everything together.  Once assembled, you can download the app on an apple or android device, and program your robot to do whatever.  Scarrax can really more -- you'd be surprised at his speed and dancing ability, particularly considering he's made from a single flat sheet of plastic.  I would say this is appropriate for late tweens and teens, although some younger children might be able to use it (1) if they're super geniuses or (2) with adult help.

text_fidelity_a:
Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players This is a very cute concept and something out-of-the-ordinary for a board game! The object of the game is to make it out with the least amount of goo on your shoe. This is represented by actual pieces of putty that you place on the board and squish with your pawn as you land on a square (thus sticking the goo to your, erm, shoe).
My kids really enjoyed it, but I can't help feeling like there are some design flaws that could have been prevented. For example, the spinner needs to be deconstructed to put away in the box. The way the board folds (see picture), the crease is over the spinner area, and with the bars on the spinner (which I like, as it looks like a playground toy) won't fit, which means you have to totally take that apart and rebuilt it each time. On that note, it isn't much of a spinner at all, but just a wheel. There is no clicker or arrow that sticks out to slow it down as it spins... it basically spins until momentum from your push wears out, sort of like spinning a top. It takes a while to finally stop on its own, which makes the game feel like it is moving slowly. I was very tempted to just stop it manually a few times, but that might bring up the possibility of cheating.
Meanwhile, I wish the goo had more colors, or at least colors that matched the shoes in the game. I can say on the positive note, the goo is very kid friendly!
My daughter lost one of the colors and it turns out she was SITTING on it and it was all stuck in her dress. I suddenly had flashbacks of when silly putty got stuck on her clothing and bed and we had to toss them both because it never came off... but this stuff comes off! It easily rolls into balls with your fingers and comes right off clothing in the process. So, definitely some extra points for that! I just wish the game board and spinner were designed a little better, that would make it a lot more fun to play (and put away!).
text_fidelity_b: Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+ The instructions in the box are lacking and the website is only slightly better. There isn't anything to download to get it to work. It works, the few times it works, via a web browser.

The device itself has a built in WiFi connection. You can, I think, secure it with a password if you want. It's open by default. You connect to it as a WiFi connection then go to its website to get it to work. I find it hangs nearly constantly. Out of the first ten tries, it worked once, each time running the same code. Here I will point out, I can't get it to go and I'm a senior software developer.

It runs on a very small surface. A sheet of 8 1/2 x 11 printer paper is perfect. It has no edge detection, so mind it doesn't wander off the edge of the table. It starts with the pen fully down by necessity, or at least I can't get it to do anything unless I fully seat the pen, which means it will touch the paper when it is set down,, so it will leave a blob that will bleed through the average paper. Indeed, these bleed almost as bad an an alcohol-based marker.

While it will work with JavaScript or Python, it provides no insight into how to use these languages, so if your kid knows Python they can learn to code the robot in Python, which just means learning its custom library. I would not go so far as to say it teaches much of anything. Hour of code shows as much, is free, and is far more reliable.

It's cute, but until the bugs are worked out, it's not worth the hassle.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+

I bought this one too go on Vacation with us in April to florida, mostly because of its footprint and portability, it is a little smaller than the 270.

Eventually I will be spending a ton on a DJI Mavic pro as I want to have a drone with autonomous flight and obstacle avoidance, but these drones have definitely exceeded my expectations and well worth the $$$ spent and are a great addition too my 7 other flying machines I have! So I highly recommend this unit!

The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up Several years ago there was a British series about Robin Hood, and my family and I have been hooked ever since seeing that series. This game seemed like a good fit for my family based on our interests, and so far it has been a good addition to family game night. That said, this game tends to be on the easy side and the replayability isn't great if you want a varying experience.

In a nutshell, this is a basic move-around-the-board game at its heart, though it requires cooperation instead of competition and it relies on a story book to further the game along. Some real time and attention to detail went into the design and it shows.

Though the game does not require following a path without turning to the left or right, it does follow a basic flow and the story book is designed to help guide and direct. That said, it essentially is a map of how to get through each step and it does not vary from game to game so once the game has been played the book could potentially slow down a game instead of moving it along at an interesting pace since previous players will know what to do.

This is certainly not a bad game. It's a good family game and is worth running through as a group. However, for those looking for replayability, this one lacks variety.
text_fidelity_b: The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up

text_fidelity_a:
B. toys – Water Doodler Portable Drawing Board – Kids Painting Writing Doodle Board Toy – Perfect Travel Toys for Toddlers Non-Toxic – Color Doodle Drawing Game & Magic Water Pens The main thing that this toy reminds me of is invisible ink, though in reverse. Invisible ink made with lemon juice (see recipe below) starts out invisible, and can be made to "magically" appear. It's the opposite with this toy. When a child draws on this board, the drawing is initially visible, but it starts to fade within seconds, and it is completely gone within half a minute. Most children like to be able to see what they have drawn, as a complete drawing. Experiencing one's drawing disappear before one can even fully finish it is an exercise in sobbing futility for most young children.

Another comparison I'd make, and not to the favor of this toy, is that it is a poorly conceived remake of the classic toy, the [[ASIN:B00000J0HG Etch A Sketch]], which is a much better choice for no-mess drawing because, with that toy, the child's drawing does not go away until the child shakes the Etch A Sketch.

In my humble opinion, this toy is more geared toward caregivers than children because of its low mess-making potential. The pens don't leak, though it wouldn't matter if they did, because they are filled with water. It is also easy to tidy up this toy because it comes in a sturdy storage case with convenient handles.

Unfortunately, this is supposed to be a toy for children. Though it is certainly possible that some children will like this toy, I believe that many more will be frustrated. For that reason, I can't recommend it.

For those who are interested in an old-fashioned, inexpensive game of disappearing ink where children are less frustrated because they can make it reappear, here is a recipe:

1. Squeeze 1 tbsp. or so of lemon juice (either bottled juice, or juice of half a lemon) into a bowl and thin it with 1 tsp. of water.
2. Dip a Q-tip into the lemon juice mixture and use it to write a message onto a sheet of white paper.
3. Wait for the juice to dry completely, and watch it become invisible.
4. Show your secret message to a friend by heating the paper (safely!) by holding it close to an incandescent lightbulb. (Do NOT hold it near an open flame!)
text_fidelity_b: B. toys – Water Doodler Portable Drawing Board – Kids Painting Writing Doodle Board Toy – Perfect Travel Toys for Toddlers Non-Toxic – Color Doodle Drawing Game & Magic Water Pens
